standard_prerequisites: Delivered card L48286 (same unit pool): an ideal generated by a countable collection of idempotents is projective as an R-module (author lemma-ideal-generated-by-idempotents-projective, source lines 2661-2683, with its complete Mittag-Leffler proof)

Context span 2685-2694: if P subset Q is an inclusion of R-modules with Q finite and P locally free, and Q is generated by N elements, then P is finite locally free with free parts of rank at most N (Algebra, map-cannot-be-injective), and P is a finite R-module (Algebra, finite-projective)

Context span 2696-2705: combining these, a non-finitely-generated ideal generated by a countable collection of idempotents is projective but not locally free; explicit example R = product over N of F_2 with I generated by the idempotents e_n = (1, ..., 1, 0, ...) with n ones
core_obligations: I = (e_1, e_2, ...) in R = product F_2 is generated by a countable collection of idempotents and is not finitely generated (each generator e_n is needed: e_n does not lie in the ideal generated by e_1, ..., e_{n-1})
By the delivered lemma-ideal-generated-by-idempotents-projective (card L48286) I is projective as an R-module
If I were locally free, the context transfer argument with Q = R (generated by one element) would make I finite, contradicting non-finite-generation; hence I is not locally free
proof_roadmap: Instantiate R and the idempotent ideal I from the context
Invoke the delivered projectivity lemma L48286
Rule out local freeness via the context finite transfer argument
